title: Accessibility Act — first full enforcement year
summary: European Accessibility Act as CZ zákon č. 424/2023 Sb., in force since 28 Jun 2025 — 2026 is the first full enforcement year. ČOI runs mystery-shopping test purchases on e-shops (whole checkout flow) and can order corrective measures and fines. Every non-micro CZ e-shop, bank, ticketing and e-book service must meet accessibility requirements now, not at a future date.
notes:
- Status: obligation live since 2025-06-28; enforcement wave 2026 (ČOI test purchases); self-service terminals transition until 2030.
- Who: CZ e-shops, banks, transport ticketing, e-book sellers, consumer-device makers (micro-enterprise service exemption only).
- Market created: WCAG 2.1 audits and remediation, automated accessibility monitoring SaaS, accessibility-statement tooling.
- Additional sources: https://www.zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/2023-424 ; https://www.shop5.cz/clanek/faq-pristupnost-e-shopu-a-zakon-c-424-2023-sb-na-koho-se-skutecne-vztahuje/

title: New Accounting Act — IFRS-aligned rewrite
summary: Nový zákon o účetnictví: submitted to the Chamber of Deputies 12 Dec 2025 with an accompanying act amending 140+ provisions; planned effectiveness 1 Jan 2028 (holds only if passed during 2026, 12-month vacatio legis intended). IFRS-aligned concepts and functional-currency accounting force rewrites across the Pohoda/Money/ABRA/Helios ecosystem and retraining for every CZ accountant.
notes:
- Deadline: planned 2028-01-01 — flagged: NOT yet enacted; date at risk of slipping with the parliamentary calendar.
- Who: every CZ accounting unit; biggest impact on larger entities and the accounting-software vendors.
- Relevance: pairs with de-skalar (AI-first accounting firm, DE) — the modernization moment doubles as an entry window for AI-native accounting service models.
- Additional source: https://www.tpa-group.cz/news/novy-zakon-o-ucetnictvi-velka-zmena-ktera-zatim-ceka-na-start/

title: EU AI Act — Art 50 transparency obligations
money_note: Fines up to EUR 35m or 7% of global turnover for prohibited practices
summary: EU AI Act (Reg. 2024/1689) requires deployers and providers to meet Article 50 transparency obligations (disclose AI interaction, label synthetic content) from 2 Aug 2026, with high-risk system obligations postponed by the Digital Omnibus to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I); creates demand for AI inventories, conformity assessment prep, transparency/watermarking tooling and AI governance consulting.
notes:
- Verified timeline as of Aug 2026: prohibitions applied 2 Feb 2025; GPAI obligations applied 2 Aug 2025; 2 Aug 2026 = general application incl. Art 50 transparency (Art 50(2) watermarking grace period for existing systems until 2 Dec 2026).
- Digital Omnibus on AI: provisional political agreement 6 May 2026, confirmed by Member States 13 May 2026 — postpones high-risk deadlines to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III stand-alone) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I embedded). Binding only upon OJ publication, expected before 2 Aug 2026 (receipt: https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/).
- CZ angle: national supervisory structure and sandbox obligations; CZ SMEs deploying chatbots/gen-AI in customer-facing roles hit Art 50 first.

title: EU AML Regulation — single rulebook applies
money_note: EUR 10k cash payment cap also applies from Jul 2027
summary: EU AML Regulation (Reg. 2024/1624, single rulebook) applies from 10 Jul 2027, directly imposing harmonised customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership and internal-policy requirements on banks, crypto firms, real-estate agents, and newly scoped sectors, under the new AMLA supervisor; creates demand for CDD/KYB tooling, UBO data services, policy rewrites and outsourced compliance officers.
notes:
- Application date 10 Jul 2027 verified on EUR-Lex (Art 90: applies from 10 July 2027, football sector 2029); part of AML package with AMLD6 and AMLA Regulation (AMLA operational in Frankfurt since 2025).
- Directly applicable — replaces much of the Czech AML Act regime; new obliged entities (crowdfunding, most crypto services, luxury goods traders) enter scope.
- Market: gap analyses against AMLR vs. zákon 253/2008, UBO verification APIs, transaction monitoring upgrades, AMLA-ready reporting.

title: Battery Regulation — digital battery passport
summary: EU Battery Regulation (2023/1542): from 18 Feb 2027 every EV, light-transport and >2 kWh industrial battery placed on the EU market must carry a QR-accessible digital battery passport. First mandatory digital product passport in the EU and the template for ESPR passports; the obligation sits with the economic operator placing the battery on the market — in CZ that means the automotive supply chain.
notes:
- Deadline: 2027-02-18 (<18 months), hard cutover, no transition.
- Who in CZ: Škoda Auto EV chain, battery/module plants, industrial-battery importers, e-bike/scooter makers.
- Market created: DPP SaaS, supply-chain data collection, QR/identity infrastructure.
- Additional source: https://www.s-ge.com/export/en/articles/spotlight/introduction-eu-battery-passport-february-2027

title: CBAM definitive regime — first annual declaration
money_note: Certificate cost tracks EU ETS price; accrues on 2026 imports even though payment deferred to 2027
summary: CBAM definitive regime (Reg. 2023/956 as amended by 2025 Omnibus) requires importers of iron/steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity above 50 t/year to hold authorised CBAM declarant status, buy certificates from Feb 2027 and file the first annual CBAM declaration for 2026 imports by 30 Sep 2027; creates demand for embedded-emissions calculation, declarant authorisation services and certificate cost management.
notes:
- Verified via EY alert on adopted CBAM Omnibus: definitive regime from 1 Jan 2026; 50-ton per-importer annual de minimis exempts ~90% of importers while keeping ~99% of emissions in scope; certificate sales from Feb 2027; first declaration due 30 Sep 2027 for 2026 reporting year (receipt: https://www.ey.com/en_gl/technical/tax-alerts/eu-adopts-cbam-omnibus-regulation).
- CZ angle: metal fabrication, machinery and construction importers of steel/aluminium inputs; CFO-level cash planning for certificate liability accruing since Jan 2026.
- Market: CBAM declarant registration support, supplier emissions data collection, ERP plug-ins for embedded emissions, hedging advisory.

title: CER Act 266/2025 — critical-entity resilience
summary: CER Directive transposed as zákon č. 266/2025 Sb. o odolnosti subjektů kritické infrastruktury: essential-service providers reported data to MV ČR by 1 Mar 2026, the state designates critical entities by 17 Jul 2026, and designated entities then owe risk assessments and resilience plans on statutory clocks through 2026–2027. The physical-resilience sibling of NIS2/ZKB, hitting an overlapping entity set with distinct obligations; compliance cost estimated in tens of millions CZK per firm (PORTOS).
notes:
- Deadlines: designation 2026-07-17 (done/underway); resilience plans + incident reporting per implementing vyhláška (in consultation Jan 2026) through 2026–2027.
- Who: CZ providers in energy, transport, health, water, ICT, food, public administration.
- Relevance: reinforcing receipt for p-0008 — the same under-capacity entities implementing NIS2 now owe a parallel physical-resilience compliance stack.
- Additional sources: https://www.komora.cz/pravni-predpis/2-26-vyhlaska-o-planu-odolnosti-posouzeni-rizik-opatrenich-k-zajisteni-odolnosti-subjektu-kriticke-infrastruktury-a-o-hlaseni-incidentut15-1-2026/ ; https://portos.cz/implementace-smernice-o-odolnosti-kritickych-subjektu-se-blizi-firmy-prijde-az-na-desitky-milionu-korun/

title: Cyber Resilience Act — 24-hour vulnerability reporting
money_note: Fines up to EUR 15m or 2.5% of global turnover
summary: Cyber Resilience Act (Reg. 2024/2847) requires manufacturers of products with digital elements (incl. software) to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents to ENISA/CSIRTs within 24h from 11 Sep 2026, with full security-by-design and CE-marking obligations from 11 Dec 2027; creates demand for vulnerability-handling processes, SBOM tooling, secure-development audits and reporting automation.
notes:
- Dates verified: reporting obligations (Art 14) apply 11 Sep 2026; conformity assessment body provisions applied 11 Jun 2026; main obligations apply 11 Dec 2027 (receipts: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-reporting, https://www.crowell.com/en/insights/client-alerts/eu-cyber-resilience-act-countdown-11-september-2026-incidentvulnerability-reporting-deadline-is-less-than-100-days-away).
- Hits every CZ hardware/IoT/software vendor selling in the EU, incl. small ISVs with no product-security function.
- Market: CRA readiness assessments, SBOM/VEX generation, PSIRT-as-a-service, 24h-reporting workflow tooling.

title: CSRD post-Omnibus — FY2027 reporting cycle
summary: CSRD as re-scoped by the Dec 2025 Omnibus trilogue agreement requires companies with over 1,000 employees and EUR 450m+ net turnover to publish ESRS sustainability reports for financial year 2027, i.e. during 2028 (date field = FY2027 reporting cycle start); creates demand for ESG data collection platforms, double-materiality assessments, limited-assurance readiness and value-chain data services.
notes:
- Status verified Aug 2026: Stop-the-clock Directive (Apr 2025) already deferred wave 2/3; Dec 2025 trilogue agreement sets scope at >1,000 employees + EUR 450m turnover, and both wave 1 (exempted for FY2025-26) and wave 2 first report on FY2027, published 2028 (receipt: https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2025/12/eu-omnibus-package-trilogue-agreement-on-eu-csrd-and-csddd). Final Omnibus I text pending formal adoption — treat scope/dates as agreed but not yet in OJ.
- Date caveat: no single EU-wide filing day; reports due with 2028 annual reports (member-state timing). Date 2028-01-01 marks start of the reporting cycle, not a hard deadline.
- CZ angle: scope now limited to largest CZ corporates (banks, utilities, industrial groups), but their value-chain data requests cascade to CZ SME suppliers regardless (VSME standard).
- Market: ESRS-lite/VSME reporting tools for suppliers, CO2 accounting, assurance preparation.

title: EU Data Act — access by design, cloud switching
summary: EU Data Act (2023/2854), applicable since 12 Sep 2025, has two compliance waves inside the horizon: 12 Sep 2026 — 'access by design' for connected products newly placed on the EU market; 12 Jan 2027 — cloud/SaaS switching charges fully abolished. CZ device manufacturers must expose product data via APIs; every SaaS provider must support exit.
notes:
- Deadlines: 2026-09-12 (access by design — one month away) and 2027-01-12 (switching charges) — both <18 months.
- Who: CZ IoT/device manufacturers (industrial equipment, appliances, vehicles), all cloud/SaaS providers selling in the EU.
- Market created: device data-sharing APIs and consent management, contract remediation, cloud-exit/portability tooling.
- Additional sources: https://www.lw.com/en/insights/eu-data-act-what-businesses-need-to-know ; https://atalayagrc.com/en/regulations/data-act/

title: eFTI Regulation — electronic freight information
summary: eFTI Regulation (EU) 2020/1056: from 9 Jul 2027 authorities in every Member State must accept electronic freight transport information via certified eFTI platforms — paper originals can no longer be demanded when a compliant digital record exists. For the CZ road-haulage sector (one of the EU's largest per capita) this is the digitization forcing function; Commission estimates up to €1bn/yr sector savings.
notes:
- Deadline: 2027-07-09 (<18 months) — authorities must accept eFTI/eCMR; hauliers that digitize first cut roadside-check friction and paperwork cost.
- Market created: certified eFTI platforms, eCMR services, TMS integrations, qualified trust services (seals/timestamps).
- Relevance: deadline receipt for p-0010 (trucking back-office) — the problem gains a regulatory trigger it lacked.
- Additional source: https://evrotrust.com/the-efti-regulation-explained-how-qualified-trust-services-prepare-your-freight-business-for-july-2027/

title: eIDAS 2.0 — EU Digital Identity Wallet due
summary: eIDAS 2.0 (Reg. 2024/1183) requires every member state incl. Czechia to offer at least one EU Digital Identity Wallet to citizens and businesses by end of 2026 (24 months after the Dec 2024 implementing acts), with banks, telcos and large platforms obliged to accept it for strong authentication thereafter; creates demand for wallet integration, relying-party onboarding, QES issuance and identity-verification tooling.
notes:
- Deadline basis: implementing acts adopted/published Nov-Dec 2024, wallets due 24 months after entry into force, i.e. end of December 2026; Commission EUDI page confirms "each Member State will offer at least one wallet ... by 2026" and launch "at the end of 2026" (receipt: https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/display/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/EU+Digital+Identity+Wallet+Home). Exact day not fixed publicly — treated as end-2026.
- Relying-party acceptance obligations (regulated sectors must accept the wallet where strong user authentication is required) follow within 36 months of implementing acts, i.e. during 2027.
- CZ angle: builds on eDoklady; banks, utilities, e-shops with KYC, and municipalities need wallet-acceptance flows.
- Market: relying-party registration and integration SDKs, KYC-flow rebuilds, QES/attribute attestation services for CZ businesses.

title: EPBD recast — building performance obligations
summary: EPBD recast (2024/1275): transposition was due 29 May 2026 and on 15 Jul 2026 the Commission opened infringement procedures against all 27 Member States including CZ — implementing legislation is now imminent and retroactively urgent. Rolling obligations: building automation (BACS) for large non-residential, zero-emission new buildings, renovation passports, solar-readiness.
notes:
- Status: infringement pressure means the CZ implementing law lands on a compressed timeline; obligations phase in from transposition.
- Who: CZ building owners, developers, facility managers, public buildings, energy specialists issuing certificates.
- Market created: EPC/certification software, BACS retrofits, renovation-passport platforms, ESG building analytics. Pairs with de-fuchs-eule (funded DE analog for landlord retrofit analytics).
- Additional source: https://oxand.com/en/epbd-2026-29-may-transposition-deadline-asset-owners/

title: EUDR — due-diligence statements due
money_note: Penalties up to 4% of EU turnover
summary: EU Deforestation Regulation (Reg. 2023/1115, as amended Dec 2025) requires large and medium operators trading cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, rubber, soy and wood products to run geolocation-based due diligence and file due diligence statements by 30 Dec 2026 (micro/small: 30 Jun 2027); creates demand for supply-chain traceability platforms, geodata verification and due-diligence-as-a-service.
notes:
- Second postponement adopted Dec 2025: Parliament vote 11 Dec 2025, Council/EP deal 4 Dec 2025 — application 30 Dec 2026 for large/medium companies, 30 Jun 2027 for micro/small; simplifications: only first placer on EU market files DDS, one-off simplified declaration for micro/small primary operators, printed products excluded (receipt: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251211IPR32168/deforestation-law-parliament-adopts-changes-to-postpone-and-simplify-measures).
- CZ angle: furniture/wood processing, coffee roasters, food producers, tyre/rubber importers; heavy documentation burden on mid-sized importers with no traceability stack.
- Market: EUDR due-diligence SaaS, geolocation plot verification, supplier questionnaire automation, customs-integration tooling.

title: Forced Labour Regulation — product ban
summary: EU Forced Labour Regulation (2024/3015) applies 14 Dec 2027: ban on placing, making available or exporting any product made with forced labour — obligation of result, no size threshold, all sectors. Practical burden falls on CZ automotive, electronics and textile supply chains, which need supplier mapping and risk-screening evidence files before customs investigations begin.
notes:
- Deadline: 2027-12-14 (16 months — just inside the <18mo forcing-function band).
- Market created: supply-chain mapping/traceability, forced-labour risk screening, supplier audits, customs evidence-file prep. Overlaps EUDR tooling (p-0012) in stack but differs in scope (supplier labour vs commodity origin).
- Status: watch signal this run — held as candidate-problem material pending a CZ demand or gap receipt.
- Additional source: https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/insights/publications/eu-forced-labour-regulation-what-you-need-to-know/

title: Green claims (ECGT) — substantiate or strip
summary: Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (2024/825): rules apply 27 Sep 2026 — blacklists generic green claims ('eco', offset-based 'climate neutral'), unverified sustainability labels and unsubstantiated durability claims. In CZ enforced via zákon o ochraně spotřebitele by ČOI; every retailer and e-shop making environmental claims must substantiate or strip them within weeks.
notes:
- Deadline: 2026-09-27 (six weeks from this run).
- Market created: green-claim substantiation/evidence tooling, marketing-copy compliance audits, label verification.
- Status: watch signal — pairs naturally with reg-accessibility-act-cz as a 'ČOI e-commerce enforcement wave' cluster; no CZ demand receipt yet.
- Additional source: https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/3c257883-bb2a-4dd9-a6dc-501d587bb34f_en?filename=faq-empowerting-consumers-gtd.pdf

title: Instant Payments Regulation — receive instant EUR
money_note: Instant payment fees must not exceed standard credit transfer fees
summary: Instant Payments Regulation (Reg. 2024/886) requires Czech and other non-eurozone PSPs to receive instant euro credit transfers by 9 Jan 2027 and to send them plus run Verification of Payee by 9 Jul 2027 (out-of-business-hours sending by 9 Jun 2028); creates demand for core-banking upgrades, 24/7 sanctions-screening rework, VoP matching services and fraud tooling.
notes:
- Non-eurozone deadlines verified: receive instant EUR payments 9 Jan 2027; send during business hours + VoP 9 Jul 2027; send outside business hours 9 Jun 2028 (receipt: https://worldline.com/en/home/main-navigation/resources/blogs/2025/instant-payments-regulation-a-key-development-for-non-eurozone-eu-countries). Eurozone PSPs already live (Jan/Oct 2025).
- CZ angle: CZK-centric banks and payment institutions must build SEPA Instant rails and name-IBAN checking; smaller PSPs/EMIs lack in-house capability.
- Market: VoP API providers, instant-payment gateway integration, real-time AML/sanctions screening, liquidity management for 24/7 settlement.

title: Machinery Regulation — hard cutover, no transition
summary: Machinery Regulation (Reg. 2023/1230) replaces the Machinery Directive on 20 Jan 2027 with no transition period, requiring machinery manufacturers, importers and firms doing substantial modifications to meet new requirements on cybersecurity, AI-enabled safety functions and digital instructions; creates demand for CE re-assessment, risk-assessment updates, digital documentation tooling and notified-body capacity.
notes:
- Date verified: applies from 20 Jan 2027, hard cutover — machines placed on market from that date must conform to the Regulation, not Directive 2006/42/EC (receipts: https://www.tuv.com/world/en/new-machinery-regulation-eu-2023-1230.html, https://www.pilz.com/en-US/support/law-standards-norms/manufacturer-machine-operators/machinery-regulation).
- Highly relevant for CZ: machinery/engineering is a core CZ export sector; "substantial modification" rule turns integrators and retrofitters into manufacturers with full conformity duties.
- Market: conformity gap audits, safety-related control system (incl. cybersecurity per Annex III 1.1.9/1.2.1) assessments, digital user-instruction platforms.

title: Cybersecurity Act 264/2025 — NIS2 transposition
money_note: Fines up to 2% of global turnover / CZK 250m under higher-obligations regime
summary: Czech Cybersecurity Act No. 264/2025 Coll. (NIS2 transposition, effective 1 Nov 2025) requires 6,000+ CZ firms and municipalities to register with NUKIB (deadline was 31 Dec 2025) and implement security measures within 1 year of registration, i.e. rolling deadlines through late 2026/2027; creates demand for compliance audits, vCISO services, GRC tooling and managed security for SMEs unaware they are in scope.
notes:
- Act No. 264/2025 Coll. adopted 26 Jun 2025, effective 1 Nov 2025; replaces Act 181/2014. Two regimes (lower/higher obligations) per implementing decrees (e.g. Vyhláška 409/2025 for higher regime).
- Self-registration of regulated services with NÚKIB was due within 60 days of effectiveness (~31 Dec 2025); security measures must be implemented within 1 year of registration — most deadlines land Q4 2026 – H1 2027.
- SME UNION reports 6,000+ firms affected across energy, manufacturing, food, logistics, digital services; many SMEs still unaware (receipt: https://www.sme-union.cz/zakon-o-kyberneticke-bezpecnosti-plati-lhuty-bezi/).
- Market: gap analyses, ISMS implementation, incident-reporting workflows, supplier-chain security clauses, municipal IT hardening.

title: Pay Transparency — pay-gap reporting
summary: EU Pay Transparency Directive (2023/970): CZ missed the 7 Jun 2026 transposition deadline; the MPSV draft law (published 26 Mar 2026) sets effectiveness 1 Jan 2027, most obligations 1 Jan 2028, and pay-gap reporting for employers with 150+ employees with first reports due 30 Apr 2028. Every CZ employer must change hiring practice (pay ranges in ads, no salary-history questions); larger ones need pay-gap analytics.
notes:
- Deadlines: directive transposition 2026-06-07 (missed — infringement exposure accelerates passage); CZ draft effectiveness 2027-01-01; reporting employers 150+ from 2028-04-30. The CZ draft is unusually prescriptive, extending into mandatory pay-system design.
- Market created: pay-equity analytics, gap-audit tooling, HRIS/payroll modules, job-architecture consulting. Foreign analogs operate at scale (Figures FR, PayAnalytics IS, Syndio US).
- Additional sources: https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/06/eu-pay-transparency-directive-the-deadline-for-transposition-has-passed-what-now ; https://natlawreview.com/article/eu-pay-transparency-directive-implementation-czech-republic-and-slovakia

title: Product Liability Directive — software strict liability
summary: New Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: transposition by 9 Dec 2026; software, SaaS and AI systems become 'products' under strict no-fault liability, and defectiveness explicitly includes missing security updates. Every CZ software vendor placing products on the market after that date carries liability exposure that current T&Cs don't address.
notes:
- Deadline: 2026-12-09 transposition (<18 months; CZ law likely amends občanský zákoník).
- Relevance: reinforcing receipt for p-0016 (CRA vulnerability reporting) — the same small ISVs that lack a product-security function now also face strict liability for missing updates; CRA compliance artifacts (SBOMs, update policies) become liability defense material.
- Market created: SBOM/update-management tooling, software liability insurance, T&C remediation legal-tech.
- Additional source: https://sota.io/blog/eu-product-liability-directive-2024-2853-saas-software-provider-guide

title: PPWR — packaging requirements apply
summary: Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (Reg. 2025/40, PPWR) requires all businesses placing packaged products on the EU market to meet recyclability, minimization, labelling and substance (PFAS in food-contact packaging) requirements applying from 12 Aug 2026; creates demand for packaging compliance audits, EPR data management, redesign services and labelling tooling.
notes:
- Entered into force 11 Feb 2025; applies from 12 Aug 2026 (18 months later), with staggered later deadlines (e.g. recyclability grading from 2030, reuse targets 2030/2040). Verified via EUR-Lex and Gleiss Lutz summary (https://www.gleisslutz.com/en/know-how/new-eu-packaging-regulation-key-requirements-august-2026).
- Directly effective regulation — no CZ transposition lag; replaces packaging directive regime, affects CZ e-commerce, food producers, FMCG and their EPR reporting to EKO-KOM.
- Market: packaging portfolio audits, PFAS testing, empty-space ratio compliance for e-commerce, EPR/PPWR data platforms.

title: Right to Repair — repair obligations live
summary: Right to Repair Directive (2024/1799): transposition and application 31 Jul 2026 — live now. Manufacturers of listed products must repair even products bought earlier; repairs from 31 Jul 2026 extend warranty 12 months; Member States must enable an online repair platform. Creates repair-ops tooling and marketplace demand in CZ.
notes:
- Status: obligation live since 2026-07-31 (two weeks before this run).
- Market created: repair-order management software, European Repair Information Form generators, spare-parts logistics, national repair-platform integrations.
- Status: watch signal — no CZ demand/gap receipt yet; revisit when the CZ repair-platform implementation is announced.
- Additional source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/common-rules-promoting-the-repair-of-goods-and-amending-related-eu-legislation.html
